walkthroughs.body_html:
Foundations in Biology — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Foundations in Biology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Foundations in Biology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which scientist proposed 'omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells from pre-existing cells)?
options: Schleiden
Schwann
Virchow
Hooke

mcqs.q: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed in 1972 by:
options: Watson and Crick
Singer and Nicolson
Schleiden and Schwann
Margulis and Lovelock

mcqs.q: Why are food chains usually limited to about 4 or 5 trophic levels?
options: Transcription happens in mitochondria where ATP is produced.
Only ~10 percent of energy is transferred between trophic levels; eventually too little energy remains to support another level.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
There aren't enough types of animals to fill more trophic levels.

mcqs.q: Where does transcription occur in a eukaryotic cell?
options: Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
Transcription happens on ribosomes in the cytoplasm.
In the nucleus — DNA is transcribed to mRNA, which then travels to the cytoplasm.
Transcription happens in mitochondria where ATP is produced.

mcqs.q: What makes antibodies effective against pathogens?
options: Antibodies are general-purpose proteins that work against any pathogen.
Transcription happens in mitochondria where ATP is produced.
Antibodies are tiny knives that physically cut pathogens apart.
They have a specific shape complementary to antigens on a particular pathogen, marking it for destruction or neutralising it.
